review.title: WebPlayerAdapter: the existing Shaka path, behind the boundary
review.acceptance: The Shaka path that exists today satisfies PlayerAdapter without being rewritten. ADOPT, WRAP, ADAPT: PlaybackController, <liberty-video>, the XState machine and the failure classifier are working, reviewed code and are wrapped, not replaced. REQUIRED: canPlay answers for a DRM candidate with a reason on the accepting branch too, because this adapter is the DRM path on BOTH targets and 'it can play it' must be as legible as a refusal. REQUIRED: getTracks reports text and audio tracks from the Shaka player, which is the first time this repository reads them at all. REQUIRED: dispose is idempotent and releases the CDM session, a hazard three separate comments in the existing player already name. REQUIRED: no behaviour change observable at the existing e2e boundary -- the critical-journey and playback-session suites must pass unchanged, and that is the evidence that this was a wrap rather than a rewrite.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on a3e1d6e. cd apps/web && npx vitest run src/components/player/web-player-adapter.test.ts -> 20 tests passed, exit 0 (re-run at 04:33 as the record for this gate); monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages with apps/web at 1026 tests, exit 0. WHAT THE 20 TESTS ASSERT. canPlay DELEGATES AND load RE-ASKS: the adapter never re-derives a protection reading of its own -- it calls protectionDecisionFor, and load() calls the SAME canPlay before touching the media element, so routing cannot be bypassed by calling load directly. A protected candidate is accepted only because WebShakaCapabilities declares a CDM; an unknown-protection candidate is accepted on the same branch, which is the state !== "clear" rule inherited from the contract rather than restated here. TRACK READING IS THE FIRST IN THE REPO: Shaka variants are collapsed to one audio row per language, asserted against a fixture with three variants sharing two languages. AV-SYNC TELEMETRY IS HONEST: readAvSyncTelemetry returns { available: false, why: "adapter_cannot_observe" } rather than a fabricated number, asserted directly. DISPOSE IS IDEMPOTENT: called twice it removes every media listener exactly once, and it completes even when a subscriber throws (asserted with a throwing subscriber and a post-condition on the listener set). MediaElementLike is structural, so the suite runs with no DOM and no Shaka runtime.

review.title: Capability routing decides the engine before playback, with a reason on both branches
review.acceptance: Which engine plays a candidate is decided before playback and recorded with a reason, satisfying the architecture invariant that already states this. REQUIRED: the routing function is PURE and deterministic -- no clocks, no I/O, no ambient state -- on the same rule ADR-003 and ADR-005 apply to ranking, so a routing decision can be reconstructed from a bug report. REQUIRED: a candidate whose contentProtection requires a CDM routes to the web adapter, always, and the native adapter REFUSES it with drm_required_no_cdm rather than falling back or degrading. mpv has no CDM; a native path that tried would be the DRM circumvention CONTENT_RIGHTS.md forbids, so this refusal is a rights property and not a capability detail -- which is why this task carries a rights-review gate. REQUIRED: the reason is recorded on the accepting branch as well, so 'why is this playing natively' is answerable. REQUIRED: routing consumes the protection state already on the session contract (PL-0902) rather than re-deriving it, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree. THE CANDIDATE-PROJECTION FINDING FROM PW-0201 IS THIS TASK'S, per gpt-architect's round-81 ruling, and no separate follow-up is filed unless this task proves one is needed. PW-0201 could not implement `canPlay(candidate: PlaybackCandidate)` as docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md §3 writes it: that client type is `{ id, providerId, source }`, it predates PL-0902, and it carries neither `protection` nor `compatibility` -- so an adapter handed one is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of returning `drm_required_no_cdm`, which is the refusal this task exists to make. The boundary therefore declares a narrow adapter-facing projection, and that projection is ACCEPTED. REQUIRED HERE: routing consumes the protection state from the playback-session CONTRACT -- the `protection` field `playbackSessionCandidateSchema` already publishes, which PL-0902 put there -- and never re-derives it; the adapter capability input is that narrow projection and nothing wider; NO SECOND DRM OR PROTECTION DECISION IS INVENTED anywhere in the routing path, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree and the reason trail would then explain a decision nobody made; and the native refusal `drm_required_no_cdm` remains STRUCTURAL rather than conditional. DO NOT change the adapter back to the older type to match the §3 prose: the prose was written on 2026-09-15 and PL-0902 landed after it, so the listing is stale and the code is right. A cross-package contract change is only to be proposed if this task PROVES one is required, with the specific field and the specific decision that cannot be made without it.

THE DRM CLAUSES ARE ASSERTED AS RIGHTS PROPERTIES, NOT CAPABILITY ONES. "NEVER DEGRADES" IS A PROPERTY TEST, not an example: fast-check generates arbitrary candidates -- arbitrary id, providerId, URL, mimeType and compatibility -- crossed with three protected states, 300 runs, and requires the native decision to be playable === false in every one. No field on a candidate can turn the refusal off, because a fallback from native to web on decrypt failure would be a system that keeps trying until something plays -- the shape docs/CONTENT_RIGHTS.md forbids as fallback logic whose purpose is to evade provider enforcement. UNKNOWN PROTECTION IS REFUSED TOO, as its own test: requiresContentDecryptionModule is written state !== "clear" so that anything which is not a positive assertion of clearness needs a CDM, and the opposite reading is the invariant-2 incident DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 4 names. A PROTECTED CANDIDATE REACHES SHAKA BY THE NATIVE ENGINE REFUSING IT, asserted by requiring both decisions in the outcome with the refusal first, rather than by reordering the preference list -- so the refusal is IN THE TRAIL. NO SECOND OPINION: a source assertion requires the module to contain no local state === "protected" or state !== "clear" test. NO LICENCE URL IN A REASON: the fixture's licence URL carries a token and the trail is asserted to contain neither it nor the host. PURITY IS ASSERTED TWO WAYS: identical routing twice, and the source may not contain Date., Math.random, process.env, fetch( or globalThis, with a non-vacuity check.

recommended.title: Production user authentication, so an account identity is not a typed header
recommended.acceptance: An account identity comes from an authenticated session, not from a header a caller typed. THE RESIDUAL THIS OWNS, IN gpt-architect's OWN WORDS FROM THE PW-0402 VERDICT: "PW-0402 does NOT establish production user authentication. The current account identity still derives from the development-header seam in non-deployment runtime. Keep that residual visible and resolve it before production-sensitive desktop routes are considered authenticated." This task is where that resolves, and until it is DONE no route may be described as authenticated. WHY IT IS P0 AND NOT A TIDY-UP. Every authorization decision in this product is built on the account identity, and PW-0402 proved the decision layer above it is sound -- which makes the identity itself the load-bearing weakness rather than one of several. On a hosted deployment the exposure is nil, because resolveRequestAccount refuses outright with authentication_not_configured. On the DESKTOP it is not: the sidecar runs on the user's machine, the runtime may classify as non-deployment, and every process on that machine can reach the loopback port. PW-0101's launch token stops an unrelated process reaching the LISTENER; it is deliberately incapable of saying who the caller is, and PW-0402 made that incapacity structural. REQUIRED: a real session provider behind resolveRequestAccount, with sessions in PostgreSQL through the Drizzle adapter, per ADR-007 -- which is still recorded as *Proposed* and whose own text says nothing below it may be cited as settled until its governing task's gates pass. PL-0405 is now DONE, so that blocker is gone and ADR-007 should be moved to Accepted in the same change, or the reason it cannot be must be stated. REQUIRED: the development-header path is not deleted -- it is the thing that makes local development possible -- but it must be UNREACHABLE from a build that ships, by the same class of mechanism NonDeploymentEnvironment already uses, and a test must prove a desktop-shaped runtime cannot obtain an identity from it. THAT IS THE SHARPEST CLAUSE IN THIS TASK: today a desktop build classifying as non-deployment would make the header the identity layer, and nothing currently prevents that classification. REQUIRED: the exact Better Auth version is pinned exactly, on the rule this repository applies to Shaka, Playwright and Tauri; ADR-007 pinned 1.7.1 and the reviewer recorded that upstream had moved to 1.7.4, so the pin is reconciled against the version actually reviewed and the hand-written migration is checked against THAT version's schema before anything is generated. REQUIRED: a refusal on an unauthenticated request must not become an oracle, and must compose with PW-0402's route decision rather than adding a second one -- authorizeRoute already returns `unauthenticated` and that stays the single answer. NOT IN SCOPE: authorization, which PW-0402 owns and which the audit found already enforced; the listener boundary, which is PW-0101's; and any identity provider requiring a commercial account or credentials the commander has not supplied -- if one is needed, that is a LAST_MILE item, not a reason to ship a weaker seam.
recommended.notes: Filed round 83 in answer to gpt-architect's request for explicit ownership of the production-authentication gap. No existing task owned it: PW-0402's own approved acceptance is authorization and its verdict names this as a residual; PW-0401 authenticates the desktop forwarder's COUNTERPARTY, which is a different service and a different caller; PW-0101 is the listener and the ruling forbids broadening it. Depends on PW-0402 because the route decision it must compose with has to exist and be reviewed first; that is a genuine build relationship and not the read relationship PW-0402's own edge on PW-0101 turned out to be. Surface includes docs/DECISIONS.md because ADR-007 is still Proposed and PL-0405, the task that blocked its promotion, is DONE.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
